messages:
ana: ran into onboarding friction this morning. the ruby sample app and the CLI produce different outputs vs curl for the same prompts. suspect SDK parity + default flags.

chris: details? which flags and SDK versions?

ana: (typo) ana: Ruby SDK v0.6.4 and CLI v0.7.0. repro: curl returns a single assistant message with `trace_id` and `policy` metadata, ruby sample returns assistant text only and no trace. CLI returns a different model variant.

morgan: can you paste the curl vs sdk examples?

ana: curl (works):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize quarterly"}],"include_trace":true,"routing_hint":"balanced"}'
```

ana: ruby SDK (missing trace):
```ruby
client.chat.create(model: 'gpt-4o-mini', messages: [{role: 'user', content: 'summarize quarterly'}])
# no include_trace param used and raw HTTP inspector shows: {"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[...]} => server returns no trace
```

tara: did the sample intentionally omit include_trace? docs show it but sample didn't set it explicitly.

ana: sample-app-ruby quickstart assumes SDK defaults include trace=true, but ruby SDK default is false. docs vs sample mismatch. CLI default is yet another behavior: CLI adds routing_hint=low_latency which picks a different model.

chris: so three problems: 1) default flags mismatch across SDKs/CLI/REST 2) docs and quickstarts inconsistent 3) routing hints missing or different per client. all lead to onboarding surprises.

morgan: also noticed telemetry: ruby SDK strips `policy` field returned by server when constructing response objects. server sends metadata in `_meta.policy`, SDK flattens and loses it. that's why the sample app couldn't display policy decisions.

chris: ouch. can you open a short repro gist and a failing unit test for the ruby SDK? if telemetry is being stripped that's a bug in the response model mapping.

ana: gist: https://gist.github.com/ana/9876abcd includes curl, ruby, cli snippets and a wire log showing server response: `{"assistant":"...","_meta":{"trace_id":"t-123","policy":"routeA"}}` and ruby client returning only `assistant` string.

ci-bot: New issue created DEVEX-4325: "SDK parity: default flags + telemetry flattening in ruby SDK and CLI routing hint drift" assigned to @morgan. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/DEVEX-4325

morgan: plan: 1) align SDK defaults to server docs: include_trace default=false on server, so update docs and sample apps to explicitly set include_trace=true when demos need it OR change SDK default to match docs (we should prefer explicit opt-in). 2) fix response model mapping in ruby SDK to preserve `_meta` fields under a `meta` attr. 3) add CLI opt to not inject routing_hint by default. 4) add contract tests (curl vs each client) to catch these earlier.

chris: +1. also add a lint rule to the docs repo that flags quickstarts that don't explicitly set server-visible flags (include_trace, routing_hint, enable_structured_output).

tara: small UX note: onboarding users often copy the sample-app verbatim. it's safer to make sample-apps explicit rather than implicit defaults. I'll open a docs PR to update the ruby quickstart to set include_trace and routing_hint explicitly and add a note about CLI injecting hints.

morgan: I'll open a ruby SDK PR to stop flattening `_meta` and to add a serializer test to ensure `include_trace` behavior is transparent. targeting v0.6.5.

devex-bot: Linked issues: DEVEX-4325, DOCS-321. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ruby/pull/54 (WIP). CI will run contract tests on staging.

chris: one more thought: add a tiny smoke-check in the sample-app CI that compares the example curl result and SDK result (text + meta keys). fail CI loudly if different. that would prevent regressions.

morgan: good idea. adding a sample-app check to run nightly against staging.

ana: thanks team. workaround for now: sample-app maintainers, explicitly pass `include_trace: true` and set `routing_hint` in the Ruby quickstart. CLI users: run with `--no-routing-hint` if you want parity with curl.

chris: thanks, leaving this thread as the record for sample-app owners and docs. :rocket:
